root_cause: The readiness probe still targets port 3000, but the new 2.4.0 image's HTTP server listens on 8080, so every readiness check is refused and the pods can never become Ready.
evidence: deployment.yaml: readinessProbe httpGet targets port 3000 while the container has run image profilesvc.azurecr.io/profile-svc:2.4.0
kubectl-describe-pod.txt: Ready 0/1 and repeated 'Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.3.71:3000/healthz": dial tcp 10.244.3.71:3000: connect: connection refused'
profile-svc.log: profile-svc 2.4.0 reports 'HTTP server listening on http://0.0.0.0:8080' and starts cleanly
kubectl-rollout-status.txt: rollout exceeds its progress deadline because the new replica never turns Ready
Dockerfile.diff: base image bump node:20.11.1-slim to node:20.15.0-slim is innocent (red herring), but the diff also shows EXPOSE moving from 3000 to 8080
fix: Update the readiness probe (and the declared containerPort) in the profile-svc Deployment to port 8080 to match the new image's listen port, then re-run the rollout: kubectl set probe port to 8080 in tasks manifests and let the deployment roll again.
